title: Ethiopian Tigray Chicken Stew
community: Tigray region — the northern highland chicken tradition
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Tigrinya Chicken Stew — the northern Ethiopian Tigray version of Doro Wat, distinguished by its unique spice balance with more cardamom and cloves, and the addition of rue (tena adam). The northern highland chicken stew that carries the distinctive Tigrinya aromatic signature.
longDesc: The Tigrinya chicken stew reflects the northern highlands' spice preferences — the cardamom and cloves are more prominent than in southern Doro Wat, and the rue (used in mekelesha) is added to the sauce. The result is slightly more aromatic and slightly less purely berbere-driven than the national version.
ingredients: ¼ tsp dried rue (tena adam) or thyme
steps: Marinate chicken 30 minutes in lemon and salt.
Add kibbeh. Add berbere, cardamom, and cloves. Toast 4 minutes.
Add rue or thyme, garlic, and ginger. Cook 2 minutes.
Add chicken. Add water. Simmer covered 90 minutes.
chefTips: The cardamom and cloves are the Tigrinya distinction — use them generously.
Rue (tena adam) gives the characteristic Tigrinya note — find it dried at Ethiopian shops.
commonMistakes: Omitting cardamom — not Tigraway without it.
cookingScience: See ETH051 for Zigni (northern beef stew) science — the same cardamom and clove addition applies here.
servedWith: With Ambasha (ETH005) for a complete Tigrinya table
healthBenefits: Cardamom supports digestion and respiratory health.
culturalNote: Tigraway Doro is the taste of northern Ethiopia — the Tigray highlands' distinct culinary identity expressed through the same dish that unites all Ethiopia, but made unmistakably its own through cardamom, cloves, and rue.
